title: Validity in first-order logic is undecidable
statement: There is no algorithm that, given an arbitrary sentence of first-order logic with at least one binary relation symbol, decides whether it is valid in every model.

formal.statement: ; NOT EXPRESSIBLE. The proposition quantifies over algorithms and over the set of all first-order sentences. axeyum has no term for either, and the statement is about the non-existence of a decision procedure rather than about the truth of any sentence, so no assertion of ours has it as a consequence of unsatisfiability.

provenance.source: authored from the S:logic-and-proof strand of the math-education concept graph; statement written here, not copied

notes: Same misuse of `open` as F:godel-first-incompleteness, for the same reason. Recorded because it is the proposition that makes `unknown` a first-class result rather than a failure: this theorem is the reason axeyum's solver trait must be allowed to decline, and it is the boundary the whole 'ladder past quantifier-free' programme is climbing toward rather than through. Note the exact shape of the limit -- it forbids a decision procedure, not a semi-decision procedure. Validity in FOL is recursively enumerable, so a complete PROVER is possible and only a complete DECIDER is not, and that distinction is what separates a reachable goal from an impossible one for this repository. Formalising the statement would need the same reflection machinery F:godel-first-incompleteness names, plus a model of computation.
